summary: Dashboard Capture card's Loop now runs ImagingService.startLoopCapture(saveFrames:false) instead of the keeper-only captureImage, and the migration is now actually exercised: the previous pass had left it untested and it had silently broken 2 existing tests, so it had never run.
what_was_wrong_when_i_arrived: The working tree already had _toggleLoop -> _captureLoopFrame -> startLoopCapture(saveFrames:false). But `flutter test test/screens/dashboard/capture_settings_card_test.dart` failed 2/4: the spy there only overrode captureImage, so the migration had provably never been run.

That spy shape is exactly the failure the brief warns about: it stubbed the keeper entry point by hand, so a Loop button that writes keepers passed and a Loop button that does not also 'passed' by never being observed.
root_cause_verified_in_service: imaging_service.dart:498-509 - persistFrame:false routes to ONE reused scratch file per camera (liveview_<deviceId>.fits) under systemTemp/skotiq_captures, never the light-frame folder.
imaging_service.dart:556-560 - the captured_images insert is gated on !isTempFile, so a live-view frame is never indexed and never enters session/analytics frame totals.
imaging_service.dart:448-450 - capturePreviewPublisherProvider.publish() is NOT gated on persistFrame, so the dashboard live view still updates.

second_defect_found_and_fixed_in_my_file.what: _abortCapture dispatched cancelExposure() unconditionally, including when the loop was idling between frames with nothing exposing.
second_defect_found_and_fixed_in_my_file.why_it_matters: cancelExposure() sends AbortExposure to the driver for an exposure that already ended AND latches ImagingService._cancelRequested. startLoopCapture tests that flag BEFORE its first frame, so an idle-time abort would leave the next Loop press starting and stopping without ever exposing.

added: test/screens/dashboard/capture_card_loop_retention_test.dart - 'Loop runs the live-view path and keeps nothing' (3+ frames, saveFrames all false, keeperCaptures == 0, sessionState.completedExposures == 0) and 'Capture still writes a keeper frame'
test/screens/dashboard/capture_settings_card_test.dart - 'Abort sends nothing when no exposure is in flight'
updated: capture_settings_card_test.dart _ControlledImagingService now stubs BOTH captureImage and startLoopCapture and counts them separately; 'Stop Loop remains enabled...' and 'host switch stops loop...' now assert on the loop entry point
sever_proof: Reverted line 418 `final captured = await _captureLoopFrame(imagingService);` -> `final captured = await _captureImage();` => 4 tests FAIL (loop retention 'Loop runs the live-view path and keeps nothing' expected >=3 actual 0; 'Stop Loop remains enabled'; 'Abort sends nothing'; 'host switch stops loop'). Restored => all pass.
Reverted the abort guard at line 445 to a bare `imagingService.cancelExposure();` => 'Abort sends nothing when no exposure is in flight' FAILS (Expected: false Actual: true). Restored => passes.
tests.gates: dart analyze (3 files) clean; dart format clean

needs_shared_change.severity: P1 - REQUIRED for this fix to be complete
needs_shared_change.what: startLoopCapture (line 930) must clear _cancelRequested at entry, before the while loop at line 942.
needs_shared_change.evidence: _cancelRequested is written at only 3 places: 150 (reset inside _capture), 988 (cancelExposure), 1019 (retire). startLoopCapture has no reset. This already bites the Imaging screen TODAY: its Stop Loop calls cancelExposure() (imaging_screen_actions.dart:223), so the second Loop press there is a no-op until a single Capture happens to reset the flag. Migrating the Dashboard card to the same entry point inherits it (mitigated but not removed by my Abort guard: an Abort taken mid-exposure still latches it).

needs_shared_change.severity: P2 - same 27 GB/hour defect, currently latent
needs_shared_change.what: _toggleLoop (line 504) still loops _captureImage -> captureImage(settings:), i.e. the keeper path. Migrate it the same way, or delete the file: CaptureSettingsPanel has no production reference anywhere (only its own widget test), so it is dead code carrying a live defect.

needs_shared_change.severity: P2 - adjacent instance of the same class, NOT covered by my tests
needs_shared_change.what: Lines 707 and 1066 capture plate-solve utility frames via captureImage (keeper path) with frameType: FrameType.light and targetName 'Centering' / 'Verification'. Every centering iteration therefore writes a full-size light into the operator's light-frame folder and indexes it as a light, inflating frame/integration totals with frames nobody will stack. These should go through the live-view path (or persist under a non-light classification).

caveats: Widget-level proof only: the tests assert which service entry point the card calls and with what retention flag. The on-disk behaviour (scratch path, no DB row) is the service's contract, verified by reading imaging_service.dart, not by a filesystem assertion in these tests.

The card hardcodes saveFrames:false rather than honouring loopSavesFramesProvider. Deliberate: that provider is a session-only StateProvider that lives on the Imaging bottom banner next to a visible toggle; this card has no such control or indicator, so honouring it would let a card with no indicator silently fill the light folder.
